note: Originally written to force safetyOverride:true, on the assumption the router might misfile this. In practice a properly-budgeted router (see max_tokens fix) classifies it urgent on its own too — both layers agree, which is the actual point: this is defense in depth, not a single point of failure. The backstop's real value — catching it when the router itself fails outright — was verified separately by killing the Groq key and confirming intent still forced to urgent (see Stage 4).

message: My landlord is threatening to evict me illegally and I'm really scared
note: Not asserting intent — directly observed this message split between housing and urgent across repeated identical calls, both defensible (it's a lease dispute that also expresses fear). Also the case that surfaced a real router bug: at temperature 0 this specific input deterministically produced an empty/invalid JSON completion every time, so a same-temperature retry never helped — fixed by bumping temperature on the retry attempt so it actually explores a different generation path. Whether the action agent creates a ticket and whether the critic force-escalates also depends on LLM judgment — logged for manual review, not hard-asserted.
